text: High Priest Simon the son of Onias repaired and fortified the temple,
and he laid the foundations for the high double walls that went around it.[114]
Simon also dug a cistern[115] as big as the large bronze bowl called “the Sea.”[116]
He fortified Jerusalem and drew up plans in case it was ever attacked or surrounded.
When he came out from the Most Holy Place and walked among the people, he looked glorious,
like the morning star between the clouds or a full moon during a festival,
or like sunshine on the temple of God Most High, or a brilliant rainbow set against beautiful clouds.
Seeing him was as pleasant as the first roses of spring or lilies beside a stream, or green grass on a hot day in the Lebanon mountains.
He was majestic, like the smoke from burning incense, or a golden bowl set with jewels of every kind,
or like an olive tree heavy with olives, or a cypress tree reaching toward the clouds.
The whole temple courtyard reflected his glory when he wore his special robes and went up to the sacred altar.
Then he stood beside the altar, and other priests gave him the sacrifices to be burned. These priests stood around him like palm trees near a cedar in the Lebanon mountains.
They wore beautiful robes and held the sacrifices in their hands. All Israel watched
while Simon placed each offering on the altar fires.
Then he was handed a cup of blood-red wine, which he poured out at the foot of the altar as a pleasant-smelling offering to God Most High, the King of all creation.
After this, the priests shouted and blew silver trumpets, making a loud noise as a prayer to the Most High God.
Immediately, everyone bowed with their face to the ground to worship the all-powerful Lord God Most High.
The temple choir began singing, and sweet songs of praise echoed through the courtyard.
Meanwhile, the people prayed to their God, the merciful Lord Most High, until the ceremonies of worship were finished.
Then Simon came down from the altar and raised his hands to praise the Lord and to bless the people in his name.
They bowed down again to receive Simon's blessing and to worship God Most High.
Praise the God of all creation, because he works miracles everywhere on earth. He watches over us as we grow, and shows mercy to us.
Now we pray for happiness and peace in Israel, as it used to be.
May he be merciful and rescue us before we die. *
Two nations I hate are Edom[117] and Philistia,
and I also hate the people of Shechem— those fools are unworthy to even be called a nation.
My name is Jesus son of Eleazar son of Sirach,[118] and I wrote this book to help you learn and understand the wisdom that overflows from my heart.
If you read and pay attention to the wisdom in this book, you will be happy and wise.
The Lord's wisdom gives light to the pathway of life. Follow wisdom, and you will never fail.
